newsitem.title: USA: Jewell says felt like "hunted animal" in bomb probe.
newsitem.headline: Jewell says felt like "hunted animal" in bomb probe.

text.p: Richard Jewell, a security guard cleared as a suspect in the Olympic Games bombing, said on Monday the media and police stalked him "like a hunted animal" and made wrong assumptions about his background and character.

"I felt like a hunted animal, followed constantly, waiting to be killed," Jewell, a 33-year-old former policeman, said in a prepared statement to journalists. With his voice breaking and tears in his eyes, he said he planned to try to find work again as a law enforcement officer.

Jewell, flanked by an American flag, called his experience "88 days of hell." He criticised the FBI investigation of him and the U.S. news media for their coverage of the July 27 bombing at the Centennial Olympic Park in downtown Atlanta, which killed two people and injured more than 100.
Jewell, 33, was finally cleared of suspicion on Saturday when the Justice Department issued a letter saying he was no longer a target of the FBI bomb investigation.

"Now that I have received the government's letter, I feel a sense of relief," he said. "After 88 days of hell, it is hard to believe it is really over...I hope and pray that no one else is ever subjected to the pain and ordeal I have gone through."

Early on July 27, Jewell was working as a private security guard near the park when he spotted a suspicious green knapsack at a crowded outdoor concert. He alerted police and helped clear revellers from the area before a pipe bomb inside the sack exploded at 1:20 a.m.
